findings.message: The noise acts only along z, and at the start the step is almost all along z. So the Next step and Full-batch step arrows lie nearly on top of each other and differ only in length. The stochastic direction change is hard to see. This is disclosed, but noise in both axes would show SGD's wander more clearly.
Before any run, the status reads 'paused'. 'ready' or 'waiting' would be more honest. Nothing has been paused yet.

Not sampled: the low end of the learning rate (0.01), batch sizes 1 and 256, and New run with a kept path. At 0.01, convergence needs hundreds of steps, and the 64-point trail limit drops the start of the path.
Near the minimum, the Full-batch step arrow is shorter than the 0.4 threshold and is hidden. Only the noisy step is visible, so there is no comparison between the two steps here. This is disclosed.
The path points are clamped to the rim and joined by straight chords. The long chords float above the bowl, and some of their segments look thinner.
The 'Next step' label wraps onto two lines in this view.
Arrows are capped at 2 long. At high rates, before divergence, both arrows can hit the cap, and then their lengths no longer show the real difference between the steps. The cap is disclosed.
